correctness.rationale: Schur/inverse-diagonal formulas for the two exact SPD matrices give a rank-one discrepancy operator with norm D. Differentiating D yields a strictly decreasing numerator in t and unique positive quadratic root in t squared; substitution establishes the sharp one-half asymptotic constant. Direct derivatives of two exact squared LOOCV losses give the strict t>sqrt(lambda) sign reversal, including the inverse-multiquadric shape map. The standalone verification code passed 2,800 exact fraction inverse comparisons, 2,340 rational derivative-sign tests and 50,000 numerical peak comparisons. The continuous theorem is algebraic, not inferred from finite tests.

originality.rationale: Primary source Lyu–Veiga arXiv:2602.10248v1 Secs 2–3, 5 defines the Nyström ridge and Rippa LOOCV landscape but does not quantify the exact two-site operator-norm amplification, maximizing correlation, or inverse-gradient interval. Bucci–Nakatsukasa–Park arXiv:2511.15583v2 treats pseudoinversion and floating-point stability, whereas here the scalar core is 1 and the error is exact arithmetic. Rippa original inverse formula is credited. Searches of the public mathematical literature did not identify equivalent statements; originality is not certified exhaustively.

value.rationale: Quantifies a genuine method-specific optimization risk noted but not classified in the motivating numerical paper. The theorem gives the complete t/regularization region in which a low-rank LOOCV surrogate points in the wrong direction; an attained operator norm gap with sharp 1/2 prefactor; and an explicit construction with full kernel tending to identity, ruling out poor original conditioning as an explanation. This is a motivated complete two-site phase diagram, not just an arbitrary sampled numerical counterexample. The two-site case does not imply prevalence in the original multi-landmark experiments, and poor spectral accuracy of the low-rank approximation is disclosed.
